bhutan/tigers-nest.name: Tiger's Nest (Paro Taktsang)
bhutan/tigers-nest.description: A monastery clinging to a cliff 900 metres above the Paro valley, reached by a steep half-day hike.
bhutan/tigers-nest.details: Taktsang is Bhutan most famous landmark. The trail climbs through pine forest to a cafeteria viewpoint and then on to the monastery, taking about two hours up and one and a half down. Interiors are visited with a guide, and cameras and phones are left at the entrance. Pack layers and good shoes, and give yourself a gentle day beforehand to adjust to the altitude.

bhutan/paro-dzong-museum.name: Paro Dzong and National Museum
bhutan/paro-dzong-museum.description: A fortress monastery beside the river and a museum in a round watchtower above it.
bhutan/paro-dzong-museum.details: Rinpung Dzong is a large whitewashed fortress reached by a covered wooden bridge, and houses monastic and administrative offices. The National Museum above it is in a former watchtower, with masks, paintings and artefacts. Wear long sleeves and trousers, and remove your hat at the dzong.

bhutan/kyichu-lhakhang.name: Kyichu Lhakhang
bhutan/kyichu-lhakhang.description: One of the oldest temples in Bhutan, said to date to the seventh century.
bhutan/kyichu-lhakhang.details: Kyichu is a quiet, atmospheric temple with orange trees in the courtyard and a story that it pins down a demoness. Locals walk the prayer wheels and light butter lamps. It is a short drive from Paro and takes less than an hour.

bhutan/buddha-dordenma.name: Buddha Dordenma and Thimphu viewpoints
bhutan/buddha-dordenma.description: A 51-metre golden Buddha statue overlooking the capital valley.
bhutan/buddha-dordenma.details: The Buddha Dordenma sits on a hill above Thimphu with a meditation hall inside the base. Views take in the whole valley. Other viewpoints in the capital include the Memorial Chorten, where locals walk clockwise each morning.

bhutan/thimphu-tashichho.name: Tashichho Dzong and the weekend market
bhutan/thimphu-tashichho.description: The seat of government and the central monastery, plus a farmers market at the weekend.
bhutan/thimphu-tashichho.details: Tashichho Dzong is open to visitors in the late afternoon after office hours, and it is lit at dusk. The Centenary Farmers Market runs from Friday to Sunday with produce, cheese and handicrafts. The nearby textile museum shows traditional weaving.

bhutan/takin-preserve.name: Motithang Takin Preserve
bhutan/takin-preserve.description: A small reserve for the national animal, an odd goat-antelope.
bhutan/takin-preserve.details: The takin is a strange creature with a goat head and cow body, said to have been created by the Divine Madman. The reserve is on a hillside above Thimphu and can be done in an hour. It is a good short stop with a view over the town.

bhutan/dochula-pass.name: Dochula Pass
bhutan/dochula-pass.description: A 3,100-metre pass between Thimphu and Punakha, with 108 chortens and Himalayan views.
bhutan/dochula-pass.details: The pass is marked by a field of 108 memorial stupas and prayer flags, and the Himalayan peaks are visible on a clear day, mostly in winter. Stop for tea and photographs on the drive to Punakha. It can be cold and misty, so bring a jacket.

bhutan/punakha-dzong.name: Punakha Dzong
bhutan/punakha-dzong.description: A massive fortress at the meeting of two rivers, the former capital and the winter seat of the monk body.
bhutan/punakha-dzong.details: Punakha Dzong is often called the most beautiful dzong in Bhutan. It sits at the confluence of the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu rivers and is reached by a wooden bridge. Jacaranda trees bloom in spring. The inner courtyards hold temples, and a guide explains the paintings.

bhutan/chimi-lhakhang.name: Chimi Lhakhang and Punakha suspension bridge
bhutan/chimi-lhakhang.description: A fertility temple reached by a walk through rice fields, and one of the longest suspension bridges in Bhutan.
bhutan/chimi-lhakhang.details: Chimi Lhakhang is dedicated to the Divine Madman, Drukpa Kunley, and couples visit to seek blessings. A path through paddies leads to it from a village. The suspension bridge near Punakha Dzong is a long pedestrian crossing with prayer flags.

bhutan/phobjikha.name: Phobjikha Valley and Gangtey Monastery
bhutan/phobjikha.description: A glacial valley where black-necked cranes spend the winter, with a hillside monastery.
bhutan/phobjikha.details: The Phobjikha valley is wide and open, with farmhouses and pine forest, and cranes arrive from Tibet in late October and leave in March. Gangtey Monastery overlooks the valley, and a nature trail crosses the floor. The valley is cold at night, even outside winter.

bhutan/haa-valley.name: Haa Valley and Chele La pass
bhutan/haa-valley.description: A remote valley reached over Bhutan highest motorable pass, with farmhouses and temples.
bhutan/haa-valley.details: The Haa Valley was closed to outsiders until recently and remains quiet. The road climbs over Chele La at about 3,800 metres, with prayer flags and views. In the valley are the white and black temples and farmhouse homestays serving local food, often with a hot-stone bath.

bhutan.name: Bhutan
bhutan.description: The Himalayan kingdom of monasteries, fortress-monasteries and an emphasis on happiness.

bhutan/paro.name: Paro
bhutan/paro.description: The valley with the only international airport and the Tiger's Nest.

bhutan/thimphu.name: Thimphu
bhutan/thimphu.description: The low-rise capital of monasteries, markets and a golden Buddha.

bhutan/punakha.name: Punakha
bhutan/punakha.description: A warm valley of rice terraces and a river-confluence fortress.

bhutan/wangdue-phodrang.name: Wangdue Phodrang
bhutan/wangdue-phodrang.description: The district that includes the Phobjikha valley and its crane habitat.

bhutan/phobjikha.name: Phobjikha
bhutan/phobjikha.description: A broad glacial valley and winter home of black-necked cranes.

bhutan/haa.name: Haa
bhutan/haa.description: A quiet western valley beyond the Chele La pass.
